title: Avey Hotel in Boston and Eric Brown's clarinet act
summary: At the Avey Hotel a conservatory student, Eric Brown, played the clarinet for money by cackling and breaking it, and Whaley later saw a white act copying him.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: MR. WHALEY: -- New England Conservatory. See, so I got him this job, give him some money. And we used to play up in the balcony, like, at the Avey Hotel. And then I had another job where I had -- I think I had a couple more musicians.
But, anyway, we were in the Avey Hotel playing, and Woods said, tell that fellow to break his clarinet. You know what I mean?
break it in half Take it --/and then he'd play with the glass. Where you at?
I'm over here. You just tell me.
I'm over here. You tell me. I'm over here, you just tell me what you're talking about.

Oh, I'm talking about at the Avey Hotel. Brownie, he used to cackle like a chicken and take his handkerchief out and weep on the clarinet. And then he'd break it, and just take the glass with the mouthpiece and play on it.
So one day, this guy sent word up, tell that guy to break his clarinet. He sent five dollars up, see. So we did it.
What was this guy's name again, Tom?
Eric Brown? You sure this wasn't Wilbur Sweatman?
No, this was Eric Brown. This was a kid going to school, going to the Conservatory.

So I -- the next day, we were playing and the same request come up, with a five dollar bill, tell him to break the clarinet, play the chicken cackle and all that. He used to do all those things on his clarinet. So one day, I think the next week, I went to the theater. The theater was right near where we worked. And I walked in there to catch the show. And who do you think was on this show? The same guy that came and asked about the -- breaking the clarinet. And here he was on the backstage there. He's coming out, making it on the clarinet with the handkerchief, imitating what Eric had done.
And who was this guy? Was he white?
He was a white fellow. He was one of the original saxophone players.

No, I don't know, that wasn't his name. He was on the B.F. Kauss that week. So I said to Eric, hey, what are you doing tomorrow? He said, nothing. I said, well, let's go to the theater. So we went down to the theater and I says, now, listen, see that guy? He's imitating you. Remember he'd send up and you used to do all that stuff? Now he's doing
it on stage and getting plenty of money for it." Wow.
